summary:
[  edit  ]
The Blob Track  TOP  is implemented using  OpenCV .
To get the results of the Blob Track  TOP , attach an  Info DAT  or  Info CHOP  to it. The Info reports the current blob IDs, coordinates and sizes in pixels. The blob ID increases for every new blob that is detected.
It converts the incoming image to monochrome (since it operates on an single color channel), but to better prepare the image, preceed it with a Monochrome  TOP  followed by a Luma Level  TOP , and adjust Black Level, Brightness and Gamma.
Typical usage is connecting a video source (such as   Video Device In TOP  to the Blob Track  TOP ).
NOTE:  can track an unlimited number of blobs in Pro and Commercial, and up to 2 blobs in the Non-Commercial version of TouchDesigner.
See also  Blob Track CHOP

Usage
There are two workflows with the Blob Track  TOP .
SimpleBlobDetector
SimpleBlobDetector  is a blob detection algorithm in OpenCV. This method will automatically be used if  only  the first input is connected. SimpleBlobDetector has the benefit of not requiring a known background to detect blobs but only returns blobs as a position and radius, meaning that all blobs rectangles will be square. The SimpleBlobDetector can also be quite slow so lowering the input resolution is often necessary. Generally this method should only be used if the background is not known.
Background Subtraction
Background subtraction will automatically be used if there is a second input connected. Background subtraction is less dynamic and requires a known background to function but it offers a massive performance improvement over SimpleBlobDetector, and unlike with SimpleBlobDetector the blob rectangles using this method are not restricted to squares only. The background subtraction method will create a binary image from the first and second input (based off the threshold parameter) and then use OpenCV to find contours and convert those to rectangles.

parameters.label: Reset
parameters.name: reset
parameters.description: Resets all tracking data and learned background data while this parameter is On.

parameters.label: Reset  Pulse
parameters.name: resetpulse
parameters.description: Instantly resets all tracking data and learned background data.

parameters.label: Mono Source
parameters.name: monosource
parameters.description: ⊞  - Blob tracking is done using a single channel. This menu controls what single channel is used to detect blobs.

parameters.label: Draw Blob Bounds
parameters.name: drawblobs
parameters.description: Draws rectangles on the  TOP  image that shows where the tracked blobs are.

parameters.label: Blob Bound Color
parameters.name: blobcolor
parameters.description: ⊞  - Determines the color of the rectangles that are drawn to show the blobs.

parameters.label: Threshold
parameters.name: threshold
parameters.description: Threshold used to create the binary texture when using background subtraction. It is the threshold of the difference between the background texture and the input texture.

parameters.label: Download Type
parameters.name: downloadtype
parameters.description: ⊞  - Gives the option for a delayed data download from the  GPU , which is much faster and does not stall the render.

parameters.label: Immediate (Slow)
parameters.name: immediate
parameters.description: Get the current frame's output. Slower.

parameters.label: Next Frame (Fast)
parameters.name: delayed
parameters.description: Get the previous frame's output. Faster.

parameters.label: Minimum Blob Size
parameters.name: minblobsize
parameters.description: Blobs must be at least this big to be tracked.

parameters.label: Maximum Blob Size
parameters.name: maxblobsize
parameters.description: Blobs larger than this will not be tracked.

parameters.label: Maximum Move Distance
parameters.name: maxmovedistance
parameters.description: The maximum distance a blob can move in one frame and still be considered to the same blob (maintain the same ID).

parameters.label: Delete Nearby Blobs
parameters.name: deletenearby
parameters.description: Sometimes (depending on the tracking method) duplicate blobs may be created. This feature allows you to delete blobs that are too close to each other.

parameters.label: Minimum Distance
parameters.name: deletedist
parameters.description: When deleting nearby blobs, blobs will be deleted if they are within this number of pixels of each other. The smaller blob will be deleted.

parameters.label: Delete Area Tolerance
parameters.name: deletenearbytol
parameters.description: Along with the distance, the area of the two blobs can be compared. If this parameter is 1, than the area is ignored. As this parameter gets smaller only blobs that have a significant size difference (between the two blobs being compared) will be deleted.

parameters.label: Delete Overlapping Blobs
parameters.name: deleteoverlap
parameters.description: Deletes blobs that are overlapping.

parameters.label: Delete Overlap Tolerance
parameters.name: deleteoverlaptol
parameters.description: If this parameter is 1 then only blobs that are completely overlapped will be deleted. As this value gets smaller less and less overlap is needed for a blob to get deleted.

parameters.label: Revive Blobs
parameters.name: reviveblobs
parameters.description: When enabled, will revive lost blobs (ie. same ID) if they satisfy all the below parameters

parameters.label: Revive Time
parameters.name: revivetime
parameters.description: The time (in seconds) threshold for reviving a lost blob. If a blob has been lost for longer than revive time, it will not be revived and is considered expired.

parameters.label: Revive Area Difference
parameters.name: revivearea
parameters.description: The area difference threshold for the new blob and the lost blob.

parameters.label: Revive Distance
parameters.name: revivedistance
parameters.description: The distance threshold between the new blob and the lost blob.

parameters.label: Include Lost Blobs in Table
parameters.name: includelost
parameters.description: When enabled, lost blobs will be included in the Blob Track  TOP 's Info  DAT  table.

parameters.label: Include Expired Blobs in Table
parameters.name: includeexpired
parameters.description: When enabled, expired blobs (ie. blobs that have no chance of revival) will be included in the Blob Track  TOP 's Info  DAT  table.

parameters.label: Expired Time
parameters.name: expiredtime
parameters.description: Time in seconds for blobs to remain in the Info  DAT  table after expiring.

parameters.label: Use Global Res Multiplier
parameters.name: resmult
parameters.description: Uses the Global  Resolution  Multiplier found in  Edit>Preferences>TOPs . This multiplies all the TOPs resolutions by the set amount. This is handy when working on computers with different hardware specifications. If a project is designed on a desktop workstation with lots of graphics memory, a user on a laptop with only 64MB VRAM can set the Global  Resolution  Multiplier to a value of half or quarter so it runs at an acceptable speed. By checking this checkbox on, this  TOP  is affected by the global multiplier.

parameters.description: ⊞  - Sets the image aspect ratio allowing any textures to be viewed in any size. Watch for unexpected results when compositing TOPs with different aspect ratios. (You can define images with non-square pixels using xres, yres, aspectx, aspecty where xres/yres != aspectx/aspecty.)

parameters.label: Parameter Color Space
parameters.name: parmcolorspace
parameters.description: ⊞  - Controls how all color parameters on this node are interpreted. The color values as treated as being in the selected color space, and are converted to the Working  Color Space  before they are used as part of the node's operation. Note that this does not change the color space of the node itself, as that is always in the Working Color Space.

parameters.label: sRGB
parameters.name: srgb
parameters.description: sRGB  color space, with sRGB transfer function. Considered an SDR color space with respect to  Reference  White.

parameters.label: sRGB - Linear
parameters.name: srgblinear
parameters.description: sRGB  color space, with linear transfer function. Considered an SDR color space with respect to  Reference  White.

parameters.label: Rec.601 (NTSC)
parameters.name: rec601ntsc
parameters.description: Rec.601  with NTSC primaries color space, with Rec.601 transfer function. Considered an SDR color space with respect to  Reference  White.

parameters.label: Rec.709
parameters.name: rec709
parameters.description: Rec.709  color space, with Rec.709 (same as Rec.2020) transfer function. Considered an SDR color space with respect to  Reference  White.

parameters.label: Rec.2020
parameters.name: rec2020
parameters.description: Rec.2020  color space, with Rec.2020 (same as Rec.709) transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to  Reference  White.

parameters.label: DCI-P3
parameters.name: dcip3
parameters.description: DCI-P3  color space, with D65 white point and 2.6 gamma transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to  Reference  White.

parameters.label: DCI-P3 (D60)
parameters.name: dcip3d60
parameters.description: DCI-P3 "D60 sim"  color space, with D60 white point, and 2.6 gamma transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to  Reference  White.

parameters.label: Display-P3 (D65)
parameters.name: displayp3d65
parameters.description: Display-P3  color space, with D65 white point, and sRGB gamma transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to  Reference  White.

parameters.label: ACES2065-1
parameters.name: aces2065
parameters.description: 1  -  ACES 2065-1  (also known as ACES AP0) color space, with a linear gamma transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to  Reference  White.

parameters.label: ACEScg
parameters.name: acescg
parameters.description: ACEScg  (also known as ACES AP1) color space, with a linear gamma transfer function. Considered an HDR color space with respect to  Reference  White.

parameters.label: Passthrough
parameters.name: passthrough
parameters.description: When selected, the color values will be used as-is in the operation, without any modification or attempt to convert them into the Working Color Space.

parameters.label: Parameter Reference  White
parameters.name: parmreferencewhite
parameters.description: ⊞  - When converting a parameter color value to the Working Color Space, this controls how it should be treated with respect to  Reference White . If the Working Color Space is the same  Reference  White, then no adjustment is done. If they are different, then the  Reference  White level (brightness) of this color will be adjusted to the range expected by the Working Color Space. For example if the project is set to have a SDR  Reference  White of 120 nits, and the HDR  Reference  White is 80 nits, then a color of (1, 1, 1), which is 120 nits in the SDR color space, will be converted to be (1.5, 1.5, 1.5), which is 120 nits still in the HDR Working Color Space.

parameters.label: Default For Color Space
parameters.name: default
parameters.description: Will use either the SDR or the HDR  Reference  White, based on the color space selected.

parameters.label: Use Parent  Panel
parameters.name: useparent
parameters.description: Will use the  Reference  White that the parent panel has selected. If the top-level panel also has 'Use  Parent ' selected, then 'UI  Reference  White' will be used.

parameters.label: Standard (SDR)
parameters.name: sdr
parameters.description: Will treat the Parameter Color Space as SDR for it's reference white value.

parameters.label: High (HDR)
parameters.name: hdr
parameters.description: Will treat the Parameter Color Space as HDR for it's reference white value.

parameters.label: UI
parameters.name: ui
parameters.description: Will treat the Parameter Color Space as UI for it's reference white value. This uses the 'UI  Reference  White Nits' value for it's brightness.
